chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The sovereign is the watchman of Allāh on earth.

key_terms.السُّلْطَانُ: The sovereign, ruler, or one with authority
key_terms.وَزَعَةُ: Watchman, guardian, or one who takes charge

ai.seo_question: What is the role of the sovereign in Shia political thought according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this concise yet profound statement from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) defines the political theology of governance by identifying the Sultan as 'the grip of God' (Waz'atullah) on earth, a concept that underscores the divine mandate behind earthly authority. This metaphor, rooted in Shia scholarly tradition, emphasizes that legitimate rule is not merely a social contract but a sacred trust where the ruler serves as the visible instrument of God's will to maintain cosmic and social order. It highlights the dual nature of sovereignty, linking the temporal power of the ruler directly to the spiritual authority of the Divine.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 332. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
The sovereign is the watchman of Allāh on earth.
